tagline: Out of Southern Pines through the longleaf, to the Army's gate.
intro: East Connecticut Avenue starts three blocks east of Broad Street in Southern Pines and winds southeast for less than three miles, in soft curves over rolling ground, through longleaf pine and past old estates and horse farms. It stops at North Fort Bragg Road, just short of the entrance to the base.

This is the Sandhills, deep coarse sand between the Piedmont and the coastal plain. Merchants once cut its pines for timber and Royal Navy masts and harvested their resin for tar, pitch, turpentine and rosin, and by 1900 most of the original longleaf was gone.

moments.title: Southern Pines
moments.text: John T. Patrick started the town around 1884 as a health retreat, and while that plan never quite came off, the town did well enough anyway.

moments.title: Weymouth Woods
moments.text: James Boyd's grandfather bought the land to save its pines from logging and named it for trees in Weymouth, England, and the oldest known longleaf pine on record was found here.
